Quiz 0001, submission s2, is graded: three items correct, two partial, one wrong. I wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`, added learning record 0003 and updated `NOTES.md`.

| Item | Verdict | Misconception | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | none | The loop is what makes an agent. |
| q2 | correct | none | The model outputs a tool request; the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | wrong | M6 | You chose "it will eventually fix the bug". Step 41 sees the same failing test as step 40, so it repeats the same edit. Only a stopping condition, such as a step limit, ends the loop. |
| q4 | partial | M4 | The answer 4 is right. Your reasoning said the model runs the tools itself, but it only requests them and the program runs them. |
| q5 | correct | none | You gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, so the model can choose its next step. |
| q6 | partial | none | The name is only part of it. The model also relies on each tool's description and parameters. For example, `check_calendar` and `check_schedule` would be ambiguous from the names alone. |

**What to work on:** M6 first. A loop that repeats the same step with the same feedback gets the same result, and it spends your model budget on every extra step.

**Next step:** trace one makerspace request through the loop and mark whether the model or the program acts at each step. Then write what would stop the loop if a tool kept failing, and a one-sentence description for `check_calendar`.

`submissions/s1.json` is still ungraded.
